text:
Marathon Petroleum stock jumped 2.6% today to $383, continuing a steep six-day rally that's added 8% since late August. The timing matches escalating geopolitical tensions: U.S. strikes against Iran pushed crude oil above $90 per barrel today, and refiners are now running at 97.4% capacity—near maximum utilization—which means higher refining margins (the profit spread between crude input costs and finished fuel sales). When oil prices spike on supply concerns while refineries are already running flat-out, refiners typically capture outsized profits on each barrel they process.

The underlying tailwind is broader: oil prices have climbed steadily as Middle East conflict risks mount, and U.S. refineries have little room to increase output, so they're selling fuel into a tighter market. The recent Trump meeting with refining executives on fuel prices, combined with news of Venezuelan oil field concessions and continued Ukraine tensions, suggests energy market uncertainty remains elevated—conditions that historically benefit integrated refiners like Marathon with significant downstream (fuel sales) operations.
